name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 2, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:01
p.m., on November 2, 2009, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 30, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dave Gove, M.V.: discussed a letter submitted to the City Council by attorney Jim Krutcik
regarding Oso Viejo dog park opposition. He stated that the letter was written before they

City Council Minutes  1  November 2, 2009
 realized the item would be on tonight’s agenda. Mr. Gove asked if an item placed on the agenda
by the City Attorney would be handled the same way as other agenda items.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem MacLean was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council heard a staff analysis and gave
recommendations for Agenda item CS1 but no reportable action occurred in Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

John Schatz, General Manager, Santa Margarita Water District: provided an update on the algae
bloom at the Upper Oso Reservoir which is causing a foul odor in the north part of the City. Mr.
Schatz announced that SMWD has added equipment in the lake to help return the oxygen levels
to normal and the District is sampling and monitoring the health of the water regularly. He noted
that the reservoir is expected to return to normal and the smell should subside within the next
several days.

P1.  Recognize City Volunteers, for their 1,000 hours of service

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Appreciation to (1) Steven Grossack for volunteer
  hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center; (2) Etsuko Liyama for
  volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center; (3) Joyce Sasaki
  for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center; (4) Karin
  Doan-Minh for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; (5) Sarah Doan-
  Minh for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; (6) Lisa Doan-Minh for
  volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; (7) Ron Kramer for volunteer hours
  at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; (8) Barbara Lekander for volunteer hours at the

City Council Minutes  2  November 2, 2009
   Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; (9) Iva Loomis for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Shelter; (10) Janie Lucas for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal
  Shelter; and (11) Candy VonPholmann for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal
  Shelter. Volunteer Sally Taylor was unable to attend the meeting (her certificate will be
  mailed).

P2.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service Club
  (Mission Viejo R.A.C.E.S)

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Appreciation to the members of the R.A.C.E.S.
  Club.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Gail Reavis, Mission Viejo representative on the Orange County Vector Control Board, M.V.:
announced that the push to privatize rat control comes from only two members of the Vector
Control Board and the District leader does not recommend a change from the current service
delivery model. The Executive Director feels that the proposed changes will jeopardize the
health and safety of the public and she drew the Council’s attention to the materials she has
presented on the subject this evening. Mrs. Reavis also announced that the Saddleback
Valley/Mission Viejo Elks Club will hold its Peace Officers and Firefighters Appreciation
Dinner on January 16, 2010, at 7:30 p.m.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: announced that the Central Committee of the Republican Party honored
resident Connie Lee on October 19, 2009, for her volunteer and activism efforts in the City of
Mission Viejo.

Jim Krutcik, M.V.: addressed comments made by members of the City Council at recent
meetings and stated that he found them offensive and patronizing. He was especially bothered
by an attempt to connect the recall effort with an item on the agenda. He stated that it is
inappropriate for anyone to speculate on unsubstantiated rumors and he requested a public
apology and retraction from those who voiced personal opinions about the dog park.

Jose Del Barrio, M.V.: expressed concern about a dog park being located at Oso Viejo Park due
to its proximity to sports fields, a school, and neighborhoods.

Dave Gove, M.V.: asked for Mayor Pro Tem MacLean’s public apology for accusing the
neighbors in opposition to the dog park of being associated with the recall effort.

City Council Minutes  3  November 2, 2009
 Dave Breazeale, Mission Viejo Activities Committee, M.V.: expressed support for the
restoration of funds for the holiday lighting program at the Civic Center (agenda item 7).

David Allen, M.V.: stated that the attacks on Mayor Pro Tem MacLean are vigilant and
unfounded. Mr. MacLean has but one vote and all actions of the Council require a majority vote.
He urged the citizens of Mission Viejo to understand the issues behind the recall and who is
promoting it.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: announced that the community is outraged that the recall proponents will
have the taxpayers spend $270,000 when Mayor Pro Tem MacLean is up for re-election in
November of 2010. She stated that the proponents are attempting to gain control of the City and
used shameful tactics while circulating the recall petition. She encouraged those interested in
joining her group "Taxpayers Against the Recall of Lance MacLean" to contact her at
norecall@cox.net.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: expressed opposition to the recall of Lance MacLean and stated that the
signature gatherers told lies as they circulated the petition.

Myron Sipp, M.V.: discussed comments made by members of the City Council at the last
meeting and stated that he is offended that his group has been lumped together with those
involved in the recall.

Valerie Maginnis, Director of Library Services, M.V.: announced that Major Brian Dennis will
discuss his book “Nubs: The True Story of a Mutt, a Marine & a Miracle” on November 10,
2009, at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at city hall. To learn more about the program, she
encouraged residents to visit www.cmvl.org.

Christine Saracino, M.V.: discussed the unfinished construction at 26992 La Paja Lane and
stated that she is saddened that there is not a way to collaborate and come together on problems
such as this. Living across the street from construction for 10 years is absurd and she requested
an apology from Mayor Pro Tem MacLean for comments he made at the last Council Meeting.

Catherine Jasper, M.V.: announced that she received the latest construction timeline on Friday
and she thanked the contractor, Mr. Bonano, for making such a good effort. Mrs. Jasper stated
that she has hope that the project may actually be completed in mid-December after all.

Bonnie Teder, M.V.: described Oso Viejo Park and the Community Center as a remarkable space
that the residents of the City share. She is dismayed that this is the spot the Council approved for

City Council Minutes  4  November 2, 2009
 a dog park and she recommended that a commercial or industrial area would be more
appropriate.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  MacLean

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waiver.

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated October 9, 2009, in the amount of $1,297,645.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated October 16, 2009, in the amount of $623,782.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Amend Technical Services Outsourcing Agreement with Baker & Taylor

  Approved request to amend the Technical Services Outsourcing Agreement with Baker &
  Taylor to an amount not to exceed $165,000 for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30,
  2011.

City Council Minutes  5  November 2, 2009
 7.  Restore Holiday Lighting at the Civic Center

  Adopted Resolution No. 09-51 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget to Restore the Holiday
  Lighting Program at the Civic Center.

8.  Revisions to Certain Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution No. 09-52 Providing for the Establishment of and Revisions to
  Personnel Policies.

9.  Investment Advisory  Commission  and  Community  Services  Commission
  Resignations

  Accepted the letters of resignation from Investment Advisory Commissioner Mervyn
  McCulloch and Community Services Commissioner Gloria Heer, declared the vacancies
  and directed the City Clerk to post a notice of the unscheduled vacancies.

10.  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 Street Improvement Project
  (Olympiad Road Resurfacing - CIP 202; Arterial Highway Resurfacing and Slurry -
  CIP 837)

  Adopted Resolution 09-53 Approving and Authorizing Execution of Program
  Supplement No. N020 to the Administering Agency-State Agreement No. 12-5451R for
  Federal-Aid Projects Between the State Department of Transportation and the City of
  Mission Viejo.

11.  La Paz Bridge and Road Widening (CIP 756/761)

  (1) Approved the easement acquisition agreements at a total cost of $87,500.00 and
  accepted the associated easement deeds; and (2) authorized the City Clerk to record the
  easement deeds in the office of the County Recorder.

12.  Proposed Huntington Beach Water Desalination Facility

  Adopted Resolution 09-55 Supporting the Construction and Operation of the Proposed
  Huntington Beach Water Desalination Facility.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  6  November 2, 2009
 OLD BUSINESS

13.  Summary Report on State Mandates

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report.

NEW BUSINESS

14.  Draft Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report and City Attorney Bill
  Curley read the title of the Ordinance.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance No. 09-277 Repealing and Replacing Chapter 8.12 of the Mission
  Viejo Code Entitled "Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance"; and (2) rescind Ordinance
  No. 93-108.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht expressed embarrassment that her short absence from the dais
  was listed in the Minutes of the last meeting (on page 13.) Mayor Pro Tem MacLean was
  listed as stating that she left because she didn't want to hear the truth but Council Member
  Schlicht clarified that she had taken a point of personal privilege.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of October 19, 2009, as presented.

City Council Minutes  7  November 2, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15.  Possible Refinancing of 1996 Certificates of Participation and 2001 Series A Lease
  Revenue Bonds

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve the selection of Fieldman Rolapp & Associates as financial advisor at a cost not
  to exceed $53,000 including expenses, Quint & Thimmig LLP as bond and disclosure
  counsel at a fee not to exceed $89,000, and De La Rosa & Company at a cost not to
  exceed $3.79 per $1,000 of bonds; (2) approve a structure of the refunding bonds that
  concentrates the debt service savings into the next two years, and (3) schedule a Public
  Hearing for November 16, 2009, to consider approval of the financing documents and
  release of the Preliminary Official Statement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

16.  Suspension of Proposition 1A - State Borrowing of Local Property Tax Revenue

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  approve option 2 to participate in the securitization program and receive 100% of the
  borrowed amount without any credit risk or recourse against City funds and (2) adopt
  Resolution 09-54 Approving the Form and Authorizing the Execution and Delivery of a
  Purchase and Sale Agreement and Related Documents with Respect to the Sale of the
  City of Mission Viejo’s Proposition 1A Receivable From the State of California to the
  California Statewide Communities Development Authority; and Directing and
  Authorizing Certain Other Actions in Connection Therewith.

City Council Minutes  8  November 2, 2009
   Mayor Ury stated that he feels there is an inherent risk with option 2 and he expressed his
  preference for option 3.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT: MacLean

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  There was no report on the Foothill/Eastern TCA.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that his office has provided an analysis of the formation of
a local or single school district, the results of which are contained in the notebook that he has
provided for the Council Members and the City Clerk. He noted that the Council Members may
need to refer to it as the matter advances over the coming months.

20.  Request for authorization to agendaize for response at the November 16, 2009,
  Council Meeting, the City’s response to a demand to cure and correct a purported
  Brown Act violation as submitted by Karen L. Medeiros

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he plans to calendar the City’s response to a

City Council Minutes  9  November 2, 2009
   cure and correct letter regarding an alleged violation of the Brown Act as submitted by
  resident Karen L. Medeiros.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed dog park at Oso Viejo Park and in
  support of a cure and correct action for the dog park vote: Jim Krutcik, M.V.; Karen
  Medeiros, M.V.; Myron Sipp, M.V.; Dave Gove, M.V.; Christa Hattem, M.V.; Melora
  Vandersulis, M.V.; and Mark Neumiller, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of reevaluating the options for the location of a dog park:
  Sharon Cody, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to a dog park at Oso Viejo Park:
  Beverly Russ, M.V.; Ron and Sherry Drake, M.V.; Dawn Gove, M.V.; Julia Johnstone,
  M.V.; Lisa Moreno, M.V.; Shirley Rhodes Grijalva, M.V.; Larry Grijalva, M.V.; Damon
  Mendoza, M.V.; Monica Mendoza, M.V.; Kristen Peregrini, M.V.; Tanya M. Pattee,
  M.V.; Christy Welch, M.V.; Dane Kovacs, M.V.; J.C. Moreno, M.V.; Lucas Moreno,
  M.V. Nora Neumiller, M.V.; Terrie Butorac, M.V.; N. Morene, M.V.; and Susan Krutcik,
  M.V.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

21.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Trauma Intervention Program (TIP)
awards ceremony and she commended the City’s own Crime Prevention Specialist Paula
Monical who was one of the TIP volunteer honorees. She encouraged residents to look into
volunteering with TIP if they are interested in supporting someone who is experiencing a time of
tragedy in their lives. She also commended Irwin Bornstein’s wife Ellen, who donates her time
to counsel victims of trauma, and Paramedic Steve Concialidi who received an award for his
mock drunk driving programs. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the OCTA
hearing on Oct 26 where she testified about the proposed bus route reductions in Mission Viejo
and how it would impact the residents. She encouraged those who may be affected to look on-
line and to please submit their own comments to OCTA. She stated that we are hoping for the

City Council Minutes  10  November 2, 2009
 option of reduced routes, rather than elimination of bus routes. Council Member Kelley
commended staff for another successful Hometown Halloween and she thanked the Saddleback
Valley Recreation Department for organizing the event. She commented on the steady line of
kids that were there to meet Elmo and Big Bird and stated that this is another thing that Mission
Viejo does that makes living here so special. She outlined upcoming events; the Farrell’s grand
opening at the Shops at Mission Viejo and the proposed Charter School informational meeting at
the Community Center. Both events will be held tomorrow, November 3, 2009, and on
Saturday, November 7, 2009, at 7:00 p.m., the Saddleback College Foundation will sponsor its
main fundraising gala for which she is co-chair. Council Member Kelley invited the public to
attend and asked those who are interested in purchasing tickets to please contact her as soon as
possible. She concluded her comments by announcing that the Community of Character word
for the month of November is thankfulness.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma reminded residents that the City's Veterans Day Ceremony will be
held at the Norman P. Murray Community Center at 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 11,
2009.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked if the City Attorney had found records relative to a prior effort
to implement Council Member Schlicht asked if the City Attorney had found records relative to a
prior effort to implement a single school district. City Attorney Bill Curley reported that there
were no records to that affect and while staff had some recollection of a brief discussion, none of
the LAFCO paperwork or historic City records indicate that there was a push to implement a
single district. Council Member Schlicht thanked City Manager Dennis Wilberg for installing
hand sanitizers around city hall to help defray the spread of swine flu. She congratulated
resident Brad Morton on the second-year anniversary of the Mission Viejo Dispatch blog. She
stated that Mr. Morton brings timely information and a community forum to those who read his
blog and she invited residents to visit missionviejodispatch.com to join in the dialogue. Council
Member Schlicht read a prepared statement regarding the efforts of a small vocal minority who
champion many causes in the City. She stated that 90% of the heavy lifting is done by 10% of
the people. She commended resident Connie Lee on her receipt of five governmental
recognitions on October 19, 2009, and Council Member Schlicht stated that our city’s greatest
resources are its citizens. She further stated that City leadership constantly putting down its
citizens for signing a recall petition is misguided and irresponsible and shows a lack of respect
for the knowledge and intelligence of its citizens. In closing, Council Member Schlicht asked
that the meeting be adjourned in memory of Mickey MacDonald.

City Council Minutes  11  November 2, 2009
 Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury stated that having talked with hundreds of people who did sign the recall petition,
there is very little ambiguity of the rhetoric and deception that was used in getting people to sign
the petition. He hopes that the proponents of the recall don’t get upset with some people if they
try to fight back. Mayor Ury announced that the Hometown Halloween was a big success but
unfortunately he was unable to attend due to a family commitment. He congratulated everyone
for the dialogue on the dog park. He recognized that the tone and tenor of the discussion is
positive and he hopes to see that continue. Mayor Ury discussed his attendance at the Microsoft
grand opening and an early opening of Farrell’s restaurant. He stated that these two new
businesses have brought 210 jobs to Mission Viejo within the course of just two weeks. He is
proud that we have no business license and he stated that is another way we differentiate from
our neighbors. Finally, Mayor Ury reminded residents of the Charter School presentation at the
Community Center on November 3 and he encouraged residents to attend or to contact him by
email if they have any questions on the proposal.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:04 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Mickey MacDonald, to Monday,
November 16, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 16, 2009

City Council Minutes  12  November 2, 2009
